transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Tuesday, November 10. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang loses $7.4bn in 30 minutes, drops 2 spots in Forbes rich list. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang faced a notable drop in net worth, tumbling from $162.2 billion to $154.7 billion, following revelations of an ongoing investigation into his supposed involvement with a Chinese spy. The resulting unrest caused Nvidia's shares to plunge by more than 7 percent , raising alarms about its market stability as broader questions emerge regarding Nokia's dealings in China and their national security ramifications. 3 contract workers drown during tank cleaning at Tata facility in Tamil Nadu. Three contract workers tragically drowned while cleaning inside a feed tank at Tata Marigold Company. The deceased, identified as Kaveri, J Akmal, and Sarath Kumar, were all from Rayakottai. They were rescued and taken to a nearby hospital, where they were pronounced dead. Authorities have initiated an inquiry to investigate the circumstances surrounding this incident. 'Injured throat with scissors': Kolkata techie's girlfriend 'can't remember' argument. Sarthak Sarkar, a software engineer, was found murdered in his rental flat in Kolkata after a domestic dispute. His live-in partner, Sanchalika Basu, and her mother, Moumita Basu, have been arrested in connection with the case. Investigators are examining conflicting statements provided by the arrested women regarding the circumstances of Sarkar's death. The couple reportedly argued over allegations of extramarital affairs shortly before the incident occurred. Katy Perry faces backlash over private show at Google-owned Wiz's Thailand event. Wiz, a cybersecurity firm under Google's wing, hosted a lavish five-day retreat in Thailand, featuring a performance by Katy Perry. However, the event sparked considerable online controversy, as critics highlighted the company's ties to Israel and opulent gatherings. This isn't the first time Perry has faced backlash; she previously encountered protests during an Australian performance. Wiz's penchant for high-profile events has drawn scrutiny from various quarters. 4 lakh guests, 150 dishes: Anant Singh's goes all out for daughter's wedding. Anant Singh is organizing an elaborate wedding for his daughter in Ladma village on November 25. The event will showcase a luxury Land Rover Defender and a BMW for family members. Horse racing will also occur, with substantial prizes for the winners to attract participants from multiple states. A wide variety of food dishes will be served, totaling over 150 options. Why some people love giving gifts but hate receiving them. Gift-giving can be a joyful experience for many, yet receiving gifts often induces anxiety due to feelings of obligation or inadequacy. Studies suggest that recipients may stress more about reciprocating than givers anticipate. To ease this tension, it's vital to distinguish gratitude from the pressure to return favors. Embracing gifts as expressions of kindness can foster a more positive experience for both parties involved. X locks TOI photojournalist's account after smog posts. Amidst rising air quality concerns, Anindya Chattopadhyay, a dedicated photographer, found himself at the center of a storm when his X account faced a lock due to smog images taken around NH9 and Lodhi Garden after Diwali. Committed to truth-telling through his lens, Chattopadhyay was undeterred by the backlash, with the Delhi government refuting any involvement in this controversial decision. 'Global capital for Sanatan': Akhilesh's big Ayodhya promise ahead of UP polls. Akhilesh Yadav has articulated a bold vision to elevate Ayodhya as the ultimate hub for Sanatan pilgrimage on a global scale. He stressed the importance of honest temple management and top-notch infrastructure to rejuvenate devotees' trust. Additionally, Yadav has committed to tackling local economic challenges and safeguarding the interests of traditional boatmen. Hegseth unfazed by impeachment push, defends Trump's Iran war as 'necessary'. Facing a growing push for his impeachment, US secretary of war Pete Hegseth has defended US President Donald Trump's military campaign against Iran under Operation Epic Fury, describing it as "necessary" despite questions over its political and electoral fallout after midterm setback. Stock market today: Check if NSE, BSE are open or closed for Diwali-Balipratipada. With the festive season bringing changes to the regular trading calendar, investors may be wondering whether the stock market will remain open or closed today, Tuesday, November 10. Following a special Muhurat trading session on Sunday and a regular session on Monday, both the BSE and NSE will remain closed today on account of Diwali-Balipratipada. Regular trading will resume on Wednesday, November 11. North Dakota son loses $100-an-acre farmland deal after failing farm condition. The North Dakota Supreme Court ruled that a man could not buy his parents' farmland for $100 an acre because he failed to meet their condition of actively farming it. It also ordered a lower court to calculate damages for his use of the property.
